Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers here; I can follow up with a short working session and sample CSVs.

1) Telemetry sources: primary measurements are anchored on request_id and taken from:
   - Edge ingress proxy logs (per-request timestamp at ingress/egress)
   - Inference runtime logs (token-generation start/stop and success/failure codes)
   - Control-plane heartbeat (router health + pool capacity) used for availability rollups

2) Aggregation window: we compute SLOs on a rolling daily and monthly basis. Monthly availability uses a calendar-month aggregation (UTC). Short blips are computed at 5-minute resolution, then converted to cumulative "unavailable seconds" for the month.

3) Credit timing: once measurement for a month is finalized (usually T+7 days for data reconciliation), any eligible credits are applied to the next invoice cycle.

4) Reconciliation: we reconcile by request_id across edge and runtime logs; if a request appears in edge but is missing in runtime it is marked "dropped" and excluded from latency SLO but included in availability counts per the rules below.

I'm attaching a one-pager and a short spreadsheet with a toy month example. Happy to schedule a quick call Wednesday to walk through.

Attachments: redwood-sla-summary.pdf, rfi-sla-spreadsheet.xlsx

Adding technical details for Maya's team — pasted below is the recommended procedural language we usually provide in contracting exhibits. Feel free to copy into the RFP response; I also added the exact formulas so procurement can reproduce the math.

--- BEGIN SUGGESTED EXHIBIT LANGUAGE ---
SLA Measurement Sources and Procedures
1) Uptime (Availability) Definition:
   - Observation window: calendar month (UTC).
   - Measurement granularity: 5-minute intervals derived from edge ingress health checks and request trace aggregation.
   - An interval is marked unavailable if the ratio of successful request seconds to observed seconds falls below 80% for that interval (this accounts for partial capacity loss).
   - Monthly uptime = ((Total observed seconds in month - Total unavailable seconds) / Total observed seconds in month) * 100.

2) Latency SLOs (per-request):
   - p50 latency (service egress): <= 120 ms
   - p95 latency (service egress): <= 650 ms
   - Measurement: latency is measured at the inference service egress (post-router, pre-client network). Retries and synthetic traffic are excluded. Cold-start events are flagged (see Cold-Start Policy) and excluded from p95 calculations if they represent less than 0.5% of total requests in the month.

3) Telemetry & Reconciliation:
   - Primary signal: request_id-correlated edge logs. Secondary signal: runtime completion logs.
   - De-duplication: requests with identical request_id within 5s are collapsed to the earliest receipt.
   - If edge shows ingress but no runtime completion: mark for availability accounting; if runtime shows completion but no edge entry, we retain runtime completion only after evaluating the control-plane reconciliation job (window T+7d).

4) Service Credit Matrix (monthly):
   - Monthly uptime >= 99.95%: no credit
   - Monthly uptime >= 99.80% and < 99.95%: 5% credit on that month's bill
   - Monthly uptime >= 99.00% and < 99.80%: 15% credit
   - Monthly uptime < 99.00%: 30% credit

5) Exclusions and Maintenance:
   - Planned maintenance: must be notified 72 hours in advance and scheduled in 1-hour blocks where possible; planned maintenance is excluded from availability calculations.
   - Force majeure, customer-caused incidents, and DDoS events (verified by router logs) are excluded per standard terms.

6) Calculation Example (toy month): see attached spreadsheet.
--- END SUGGESTED EXHIBIT LANGUAGE ---

I also added a note on sampling rates: we sample 100% of production requests for availability, but for latency analytics we use full request IDs and compute distribution summaries (no downsampling at the edge).

Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — answers below and I've attached a short reconciliation playbook and a tiny anonymized sample set.

1) Availability denominator: yes — requests seen at edge but missing runtime completion are counted toward observed seconds and therefore affect availability. For latency SLOs we only include requests with successful runtime completion. That language will be explicit in the exhibit.

2) Cold-start threshold: by default we flag a request as a cold-start if time-to-first-token > 450 ms. This threshold was chosen from production distributions; we exclude cold-starts from p95 if they make up < 0.5% of total requests in the calendar month. We can make the threshold configurable per-customer if you prefer.

3) Sample logs: attached as a small JSONL with 1,200 anonymized request events and a README describing each field and the reconciliation script (python). We also included a pre-computed toy-month CSV showing monthly observed seconds, unavailable seconds, computed uptime, and the resulting credit.

Attachments: reconciliation-playbook.md, sample-sla-logs.jsonl (anonymized), sample-credit-calculation.csv
